## Description
&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;2 K+(aq) + 2H&lt;sub&gt;2&lt;/sub&gt;O(l) + 2e− → H&lt;sub&gt;2&lt;/sub&gt;(g) + 2 KOH(aq)&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;2 Cl– — 2e− → Cl&lt;sub&gt;2&lt;/sub&gt;(g)&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Membrane Cell Electrolysis&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;This modern, energy-efficient method involves the electrolysis of a concentrated &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Potassium Chloride (KCl) brine solution. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Brine Preparation: High-purity potassium chloride is dissolved in demineralized water. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Impurities like calcium and magnesium are strictly removed to prevent membrane fouling.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Electrolysis: The purified brine is fed into an electrolytic cell divided by a selective &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;cation-exchange membrane (e.g., Nafion).&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;- Anode Reaction: Chloride ions (Cl−) are oxidized to form Chlorine gas (Cl2).&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;- Cathode Reaction: Water is reduced to form Hydrogen gas (H2) and hydroxide ions (OH−).&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;- Ion Migration: Potassium ions (K+) migrate through the membrane from the anode compartment&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;  to the cathode compartment, where they combine with hydroxide ions to form KOH. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Concentration: The resulting dilute KOH solution (~30%) is concentrated in multi-effect &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;evaporators to commercial strengths (typically 45–50% for liquid lye). &#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Solidification (Optional): To produce flakes or pellets, the concentrated solution is &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;cooled and solidified in flaker units. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;
